thread:
maya: heads-up — I'm prototyping a microburst-aware canary split for /v1/generate. goal: avoid a tiny canary causing short RPS spikes when sampling changes (retries + untraced clients). thoughts?

ajay: sounds good. current weighted sampler is header-hash based so a sudden config flip can move lots of clients. we saw this with the last 3% canary. :grimacing:

maya: exact problem. my idea: apply a smoothing layer that enforces a max delta per-second and an exponential decay so effective pct moves gradually. also emit a "smoothed_pct" telemetry metric. config sketch:```json
{
  "route": "/v1/generate",
  "canary": {
    "target_pct": 5,
    "smoothing": {"type": "exp_decay", "half_life_s": 120},
    "max_delta_per_sec": 0.5
  }
}```

lee: would prefer a leaky-bucket approach for per-client churn too. smoothing + bucket = avoid short bursts and also stop phase shift when many clients reconnect. also we need to tag spans with "canary_bucket" so traces split in dashboards.

sam: console UX request: show both target_pct and effective_smoothed_pct + a small forecast graph (1m/5m) and an event line when config changed. ops should be able to toggle smoothing off for emergency rollbacks.

toni: quota question — if canary consumes quota unexpectedly (e.g., tenant-level rate limits), how do we reconcile? fallback should preserve canary sampling but route to fallback backend, not just drop traffic. we need a guardrail in routing policy to avoid cascading quota failures.

ajay: agree. also need a dashboard card showing "canary pressure" — rate vs expected rate by bucket, plus high-cardinality label for path+canary_id. don't want to blow up metrics cost though. maybe sample 1:100 for high-res metrics.

maya: good call on sampling. plan: emit high-res telemetry for first 60s after a config change, then downsample. telemetry flags: "canary_event", "smoothed_pct", "observed_pct_by_bucket".

deploy-bot: canary config diff ready for stage, applying smoothing defaults: half_life_s=90, max_delta_per_sec=1.0. will run 30m smoke before prod rollout.

lee: one more: edge case where header overrides are present (X-Canary-Force). smoothing should respect forced overrides but still count toward telemetry and quota; maybe mark as "forced" so console filters.

maya: yep — preserve explicit overrides (force, admin) but surface them separately in the UI and telemetry. tagging: forced=true.

sam: will put a small mockup in /design/canary-smoothing.svg and a ticket for the dashboard card.

maya: ok rolling; putting PR up. @ajay can you review the sampling impl (particularly the bucket decay math)?

ajay: will review today. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks — will post rollout notes when stage smoke completes.
